newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian government gives budget details.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian government gives budget details.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Tuesday that its budget expenditures were planned at 6.4 billion litas next year with a deficit of 596 million litas or 1.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"Under the economic memorandum with the International Monetary Fund, the budget deficit cannot exceed two percent of GDP," the government press office said in a statement.
It was confirming the details of the budget, which was discussed by the cabinet on Monday.
The budget was unveiled as Lithuania gets set for the first round of a parliamentary election on October 20.

The ruling former Communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party are expected to be defeated and be replaced by a coalition including the right-wing Homeland Union of independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis.
The budget foresees inflation of 16 percent in 1997 and a rise in GDP of four to five percent.
The government last year tapped international financial markets to fund a deficit of 700 million litas.
